jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description

Deen Capital is a quantitative investment manager specializing in U.S. public equities, combining data-driven research with an ethics lens informed by Islamic investing principles. The firm uses systematic, rules-based multi-factor models—such as quality, value, momentum, and profitability—to guide stock selection and risk management. Deen Capital applies Islamic-principled screens to avoid businesses that conflict with Islamic ethics and to limit exposure to excessive leverage and interest-centric activities. Its investment process emphasizes risk-aware portfolio construction, diversification, liquidity considerations, and disciplined drawdown management, supported by transparent and continuously tested research. Deen Capital serves investors and advisors seeking U.S. equity exposure managed with quantitative rigor and faith-aligned values.

Role Description

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a full-time, remote role responsible for setting and executing the firm’s technology vision in support of quantitative investment and operations. The CTO will lead the design, development, and maintenance of software systems that power research, portfolio construction, trading infrastructure, and risk analytics. Day-to-day responsibilities include overseeing technical architecture, guiding product development roadmaps, and ensuring robust, secure, and scalable systems across the firm’s technology stack. The CTO will manage technology projects end-to-end, collaborate closely with investment, operations, and compliance teams, and establish best practices for documentation, testing, and deployment. This role also involves developing long-term IT strategy, vendor and cloud platform selection, and building a high-performing technical culture aligned with Deen Capital’s values.

Establish long-term technology vision, priorities, and investment plans.
Align technology initiatives with corporate and business objectives.
Evaluate emerging technologies and opportunities for innovation.
Advise the CEO and Executive Leadership Team on technology strategy.

2. Engineering Leadership & Product Technology Lead Software Engineering and Technology teams.
Establish engineering standards, development methodologies, and best practices.

Improve software development quality, velocity, and predictability.

4. Cybersecurity & Technology Risk Management Establish comprehensive cybersecurity and information security strategies.
Oversee technology risk management and security controls.
Ensure systems meet applicable privacy, security, and compliance requirements.
Monitor cybersecurity threats, vulnerabilities, and technology risks.
Develop incident response, business continuity, and disaster recovery strategies.

5. Data, Artificial Intelligence & Analytics Develop enterprise data and analytics strategies.
Oversee data platforms, data engineering, and business intelligence capabilities.
Identify opportunities to leverage Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning.

This is a broad, hands-on operational leadership role in a lean nonprofit setting, not an infrastructure specialty. Success in this role requires balancing strategy, service delivery, vendor management, operational leadership, and technical decision-making. While technical credibility is important, the role is not intended to personally perform all engineering, administration, or support work. Instead, the Director is responsible for ensuring successful outcomes through a combination of internal staff, managed service partners, and other technology vendors.

We are looking for a leader who combines technical credibility with strong people leadership, clear communication, sound judgment, and a commitment to excellent service.

You will build trusted relationships with business owners and internal stakeholders, help teams navigate technology and process changes, simplify and modernize our technology environment, strengthen the IT team and its operating practices, and ensure technology effectively supports HRC’s mission.

IT Leadership & Modernization
Develop and execute an IT operations and modernization roadmap aligned with organizational priorities, informed by strong partnerships with program owners and internal stakeholders.
Serve as the senior technical advisor for IT operations, evaluating technical options, dependencies, risks, and vendor recommendations.
Lead efforts to simplify legacy and overlapping technologies and advance a secure, cloud-first operating environment.

IT Operations & Service Delivery
Lead day-to-day IT operations across identity and access, endpoints, cloud and infrastructure, productivity and collaboration platforms, and IT-managed enterprise applications.
Ensure effective delivery of technology services through a combination of internal staff, managed service providers, security partners, and technology vendors, establishing clear ownership, accountability, and service expectations.
Establish and mature IT service management practices, including incident, problem, change, knowledge, and asset management, with clear service standards, accountability, and governance. Ensure technology changes are communicated, documented, and managed to reduce operational risk and improve coordination across internal teams and technology partners.
Drive root-cause analysis and durable resolution of recurring technical and service issues.
Lead technical planning and execution for migrations, integrations, upgrades, consolidation, and retirement of legacy technologies.
Ensure technology services are secure, reliable, and operationally ready, including appropriate lifecycle management, patching, backup, and disaster recovery.
Ensure reliable technology and AV support for hybrid meetings, Board meetings, and major organizational events through appropriate planning, resourcing, thorough testing, and coordination of internal and external support resources, providing hands-on support when necessary.

Vendor Management & Cybersecurity
Serve as the primary owner of managed service and key technology partner relationships, establishing clear service expectations, governance processes, reporting, escalation paths, and accountability for outcomes.
Evaluate vendor performance, service quality, and value realization, making recommendations regarding service improvements, scope changes, or provider transitions when appropriate.
Manage IT contracts, licensing, renewals, and technology operating expenditures within approved budgets.
Partner with fractional CISO and cybersecurity service providers to operationalize security controls, incident response, vulnerability remediation, data protection, and risk-reduction priorities.

Lead, coach, and develop the internal IT team, setting clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, communication, customer service, and follow-through.
Assess team capabilities and recommend appropriate staffing, role design, training, and use of external expertise.
Communicate technical issues, risks, options, and changes clearly to staff, leadership, and non-technical stakeholders to reduce change management challenges

At least 10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years managing IT operations, service delivery, or comparable enterprise technology functions.
Demonstrated leadership experience managing across multiple IT domains, including identity and access, endpoint management, cloud/infrastructure, enterprise applications, and end-user technology services.
Strong working knowledge of modern identity and endpoint management, including experience supporting both Windows and macOS environments.
Experience managing cloud-based productivity, collaboration, and SaaS environments, including Microsoft 365 and/or Google Workspace.
Strong IT service management experience, particularly incident, problem, change, knowledge, and asset management, with demonstrated success improving service quality and resolving recurring issues.
Proven experience managing MSPs and technology vendors, including service levels, escalations, root-cause analysis, remediation, contracts, and performance accountability.
Experience working with cybersecurity teams or providers to implement security requirements and address operational risks, including identity and endpoint security, vulnerability remediation, incident response, and data protection.

Experience implementing technology roadmaps and managing complex migrations, modernization efforts, or other significant technology initiatives, including stakeholder engagement, communication, and organizational adoption.

Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues, risks, decisions, and expectations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

Experience in nonprofit, advocacy, or other mission-driven organizations.
Knowledge of or interest in LGBTQ+ issues, and a demonstrated commitment to a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace.

new_jobs.title: Director Superconducting Technology Architect
new_jobs.description:
The Superconducting Technology Architect is a Director-level technical leadership role within the GF Labs Technology Architecture organization. This role defines and advances foundry platforms for superconducting qubits, Josephson-junction digital logic, cryogenic control and readout, and related integration. The position requires deep technical expertise, platform leadership, and the ability to translate emerging system requirements into scalable, manufacturable technologies.

Job Summary

The Superconducting Technology Architect leads the definition, development, and delivery of superconducting quantum and digital technologies and associated customer programs. The position integrates device, process, design, test, packaging, foundry operations, and program execution; guides internal and external R&D; and serves as a senior technical and customer-facing authority for GF leadership and partners.

Essential Responsibilities

Develop and influence long-term roadmaps for superconducting qubits, SFQ-family digital logic, cryogenic control and readout, parametric amplifiers, interconnect, and packaging.
Translate customer and system requirements into materials, process flows, device structures, design rules, PDK content, test vehicles, and acceptance criteria.
Shape manufacturable qubit technologies spanning Josephson junctions, resonators, couplers, readout, low-loss materials and interfaces, coherence, fidelity, variability, and yield.
Define scalable digital platforms, including RSFQ, ERSFQ/eSFQ, RQL, and AQFP, addressing junction uniformity, timing, wiring, inductance, power, memory, thermal budgets, and cryogenic I/O.
Lead process integration, experiments, simulations, tape-outs, cryogenic characterization, technology transfer, qualification, and new-product introduction across superconducting logic, qubits, cryo-CMOS, multi-chip modules, TSVs, flip-chip, and heterogeneous integration.
Build and govern internal and external development programs with customers, universities, research organizations, government laboratories, suppliers, and startups, including technical scope, proposals and estimates, milestones, schedules, budgets, IP, and transition plans.
Lead multidisciplinary engineering and program teams; recruit and mentor talent; drive quality, schedule, budget, and customer commitments; and communicate architecture choices, execution status, risks, and investment priorities to customers and GF executives.
Drive foundry operational improvement through cycle-time reduction, SPC and control-plan maturity, manufacturing systems, process quality, program reviews, and schedule-risk reduction.
Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.

Required Qualifications

Education: MS or PhD in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Materials Science, or a related discipline.
Years of Experience: 15+ years in semiconductor technology, superconducting electronics, quantum hardware, or advanced process integration, including leadership of complex technology programs.
Deep expertise in Josephson-junction devices, superconducting qubits and/or digital logic, cryogenic operation, RF/microwave circuits, materials and interface loss, and device-to-system tradeoffs.
Demonstrated success translating architectures into foundry processes and transferring technologies from research into fabrication, qualification, or manufacturing, with ownership of quality, schedule, budget, and customer deliverables.
Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary engineering and program organizations and strategic collaborations across customers, research organizations, suppliers, startups, and matrixed internal functions.
Percentage of travel: 20%.

Preferred Qualifications

PhD with industrial experience in superconducting qubits, superconducting digital electronics, Josephson-junction fabrication, or cryogenic system integration.
Experience with transmon-class qubits, microwave resonators, control/readout, parametric amplifiers, decoherence mechanisms, and cryogenic measurement.
Experience with SFQ-family circuit design, simulation, layout, timing, and 3D electromagnetic modeling; familiarity with RQL is beneficial.
Knowledge of superconducting materials and junction processes, multi-chip modules, thermal or superconducting TSVs, flip-chip interconnect, heterogeneous integration, cryo-CMOS, cryocoolers, wafer-scale integration, and cryogenic packaging.
Experience with proposal development, technical basis-of-estimate, integrated schedules, Agile execution, manufacturing systems, SPC, control plans, and customer or executive program reviews.
